# Garden Log March

## Sowings
I sowed the first tomato seeds on 12 March and put the tray on the windowsill above the kitchen sink, which gets the best light in the flat. I used a cherry variety and a beefsteak type, two seeds per cell, and thinned them once the first true leaves showed. The chitted potatoes went into egg boxes in the shed to keep the shoots short and strong, and I plan to plant them out in the second week of April. I also started broad beans in deep pots, since they hate being moved once the roots fill the space. Soil temperature in the raised bed read 8 C on the 20th, still too cold for direct sowing, so I held off on the carrots.

## Observations
The windowsill tray germinated unevenly, which I put down to cold nights by the glass. I moved it back a few centimetres and the stragglers caught up within a week. The chitted potatoes are showing short green shoots and no mould, so the shed is dry enough. Broad beans are up and look sturdy. The bed is still wet from the March rain and the soil clumps when squeezed, a sign I should wait before working it. Slugs are already active around the herb pots.

## Notes
Last frost is expected around 5 May here, so nothing tender goes outside before then without a cover. I have fleece ready for the potatoes if a cold snap comes. Next tasks are pricking out the tomatoes into individual pots and topping up the raised bed with compost.
